prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 250px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 168px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 105px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 1420px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 70px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [185, 95, 85, 275, 70] · table 711×906px · row heights [36, 176, 129, 129, 129, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 351px
Design r1C: widths [170, 88, 78, 130, 66] · table 533×1975px · row heights [36, 385, 315, 292, 292, 315, 339] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 16 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 173px
Design r2A: widths [172, 104, 88, 206, 70] · table 641×1185px · row heights [36, 222, 176, 176, 176, 199, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 281px
Design r2B: widths [156, 98, 84, 168, 70] · table 577×1464px · row heights [36, 269, 222, 222, 222, 246, 246] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 217px
Design r2C: widths [166, 102, 88, 262, 72] · table 691×929px · row heights [36, 176, 129, 129, 153, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 331px
Design r3A: widths [140, 88, 80, 204, 64] · table 577×1185px · row heights [36, 222, 176, 176, 176, 199, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 217px
Design r3B: widths [156, 92, 84, 250, 68] · table 651×976px · row heights [36, 176, 153, 153, 153, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 291px
Design r3C: widths [148, 90, 84, 340, 66] · table 729×720px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 106, 106, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 369px

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}
